Unit A — Length
CS 5.1  ·  LS 5.1.1
1

Measuring Big and Small

🎨mm & cm
🎨cm & m
🎨m & km

Aina, Danish and their robot friend Milli want to build a treehouse by their longhouse in Sarawak. First, they must learn to measure!

Danish measured a tiny ladybird on a pitcher plant in millimetres (mm). Aina measured her height in metres (m). Milli measured the road to school along the Sarawak River in kilometres (km).

"Small things need small units. Big things need big units!" said Milli.

🎨The mm–cm–m–km ladder
km → m → cm → mm. Going down: ×10, ×100, ×1000. Going up: ÷10, ÷100, ÷1000.
10 mm = 1 cm  ·  100 cm = 1 m  ·  1000 m = 1 km

LS 5.1.2 – 5.1.6
2

Building With Numbers

🎨Adding & subtracting planks
🎨Multiplying & dividing ribbon

Aina joined two planks for their longhouse-style treehouse: 1.2 m + 0.8 m = 2 m. Then she trimmed one: 1 m − 0.35 m = 0.65 m. Fractions work too: ½ m = 50 cm.

Ribbon needed to wrap a Gawai gift box: Ribbon = (4 × height) + (2 × width) + (2 × length). If a 3 m ribbon is shared equally to make 4 bows: 3 m ÷ 4 = 75 cm. Each bow is made using 75 cm of ribbon.

➕➖ Add & Subtract: Make the units the same first.
✖️ Multiply: Make the total length bigger by repeating equal lengths.
➗ Divide: Share a length equally into equal parts.

Think It Through

📐 Math Facts
10 mm = 1 cm
100 cm = 1 m
1000 m = 1 km
Add/subtract: match units first.
Ribbon length = (4 × height) + (2 × width) + (2 × length).
📖 Word Bank
lengthconvertmillimetre centimetremetrekilometre instrument
💭 Reflection
  • Which unit would you use to measure your pencil?
  • Which unit would you use to measure your classroom?
  • Which unit would you use to measure the distance to school?
  • What was tricky about converting units today?
🤔 Let's Think
  • Why do we need different units for length instead of just one?
  • If you multiply a length by a number bigger than 1, will it get longer or shorter? Why?
  • Can two objects have the same length but look different? Give an example.
Math Value 🌟 Accuracy — Careful measuring helps us get the correct answer. Always measure with precision.

Unit B — Mass
CS 5.2  ·  LS 5.2.1
1

How Heavy Is It?

🎨The Kitchen Scale
images/p12_mass_scale.png
Prompt M1 — see prompt pack

Milli turned into a kitchen scale! Aina weighed flour for a Sarawak layer cake: 500 g. Danish weighed a watermelon: 3 kg.

"For light things we use grams (g). For heavy things we use kilograms (kg)," said Milli.

⚖️ 1000 g = 1 kg. g → kg: divide by 1000. kg → g: multiply by 1000.
Chapter 5 — Measurement · Unit B: Mass
Chapter 5 · Measurement
⚖️
Unit B — Mass
LS 5.2.2 – 5.2.5
2

Packing & Baking

🎨Packing the Camping Bag & Scaling a Recipe
images/p13_mass_recipe.png
Prompt M2 — see prompt pack

Aina packed a woven cane backpack for a family camping trip in the Sarawak rainforest: rice 1.5 kg + oatmeal 0.8 kg = 2.3 kg total. She checked the bag's 3 kg limit before adding more.

For a bigger Sarawak layer cake, Milli helped Aina multiply every ingredient by 2. To share dough into 4 balls, they divided the mass by 4.

➕➖✖️➗ Add/subtract mass with matching units. Multiply to scale up a recipe; divide to share it equally.

Unit C — Volume of Liquid
CS 5.3  ·  LS 5.3.1
1

How Much Can It Hold?

🎨The Juice Jug
images/p14_volume_jug.png
Prompt V1 — see prompt pack

Milli turned into a measuring jug! In their cosy longhouse kitchen, Danish poured orange juice: 250 ml. Aina filled a big jug: 2 litres (ℓ).

"For small amounts we use millilitres (ml). For bigger amounts we use litres (ℓ)," said Milli.

🥤 1000 ml = 1 ℓ. ml → ℓ: divide by 1000. ℓ → ml: multiply by 1000.
Chapter 5 — Measurement · Unit C: Volume of Liquid
Chapter 5 · Measurement
🥤
Unit C — Volume of Liquid
LS 5.3.2 – 5.3.5
2

Fruit Punch Party!

🎨Mixing & Sharing Fruit Punch
images/p15_volume_punch.png
Prompt V2 — see prompt pack

Aina mixed 1 ℓ orange juice + 500 ml mango juice = 1.5 ℓ of punch for their Gawai celebration. After the party, from 1.5 ℓ only 1.2 ℓ was left over.

To share 1.2 ℓ equally into 6 cups, they divided: 1.2 ℓ ÷ 6 = 200 ml each cup.

To make a bigger batch, they multiplied every amount by 2.

➕➖✖️➗ Add/subtract volume with matching units. Multiply to make more; divide to share equally.

Think It Through

📐 Math Facts
1000 ml = 1 ℓ
Add/subtract: match units first.
Divide volume to share equally; multiply to make it bigger.
📖 Word Bank
volumecapacitymillilitre litrecontainershare equally
💭 Reflection
  • Name a drink container at home that holds about 1 litre.
  • Would you measure a spoon of syrup in ml or ℓ? Why?
  • What was tricky about volume word problems today?
🤔 Let's Think
  • What is the difference between "volume" and "capacity"?
  • If you pour the same 1 litre of water into a tall thin glass and a short wide bowl, does the AMOUNT change? Explain.
  • Why is it useful to know how to share liquid equally among friends?
Math Value 🌟 Responsibility — Measure only what you need. Using water and other liquids wisely helps reduce waste.
